chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khishab, from Al-Yazid ibn Ishaq al-Sha'r, from Harun ibn Hamz al-Ghanawi, from Al-Ala' ibn A'ayn, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

What is the proof against one who falsely claims this authority? He said: There are three signs of proof; if they do not all exist in one man, he is not the possessor of this authority: that he be the closest of people to the one whose heart it is, that he possess the armaments of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and that he be the possessor of the clear testament, such that when the city is entered, the common people and children ask: To whom did Fulan bequeath? They say: To Fulan.

key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: Proof or evidence, referring to the definitive proof of God on earth
key_terms.سِلَاحُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The armaments/weapons of the Prophet, symbolizing inherited authority

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs that prove someone is the true Imam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents these three criteria—spiritual proximity, possession of the Prophet's armaments, and public testament—as the definitive proof for the true Imam, distinguishing him from false claimants. This hadith underscores the Shia concept of 'Nass' (designation) combined with tangible signs, ensuring that the Imam's authority is recognized by both the elite and the common people, including children, thereby establishing an unbroken chain of legitimacy from the Prophet.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-99 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Musa al-Khishab, on the authority of Al-Yazid ibn Ishaq She’r, on the authority of Harun ibn Hamzih al-Qanavi that Abdul Ali ibn A’ayn said, “I asked as-Sadiq (MGB)

about the way to disprove one who falsely claims to be a Trustee of the Divine Leader. The Imam (MGB) said, ‘There are three signs which should all exist in anyone who truly claims to be a Trustee of the Divine Leader. He should be the closest to the Divine Leader. He should possess the Prophet’s armaments and he should be so clearly the one declared by the Divine Leader to be his Trustee that when you enter the town and ask the children or the common people about whom the Divine Leader has established as his Trustee, everyone refers to him (MGB).’”
